Based on the error log, a segmentation fault occurs during the `test_out_of_bounds` test for the EEPROM driver. This test runs in user mode and attempts an out-of-bounds write, which should be caught and result in an error. The segmentation fault indicates that the bounds check is failing, likely due to an issue in the system call validation layer when handling memory buffer sizes.

The problem lies in the `K_SYSCALL_MEMORY_SIZE_CHECK` macro in `include/zephyr/internal/syscall_handler.h`. This macro is used to validate buffer sizes passed to system calls. When the `size` argument is a signed type that is narrower than `uintptr_t` (e.g., `int` on a 64-bit system), a negative value is not correctly sign-extended during type promotion. This causes the check to fail to identify a negative size, treating it as a large positive value, which can lead to memory corruption and segmentation faults.

The fix is to explicitly cast the `size` argument to `intptr_t` before casting it to `uintptr_t`. This ensures that if `size` is a negative value of a smaller signed type, it will be properly sign-extended to the width of a pointer, allowing the check to correctly identify it as invalid.

Here is the required fix:

include/zephyr/internal/syscall_handler.h
<<<<<<<< SEARCH
#define K_SYSCALL_MEMORY_SIZE_CHECK(ptr, size) \
	(((uintptr_t)(ptr) + (size)) >= (uintptr_t)(ptr))
========
#define K_SYSCALL_MEMORY_SIZE_CHECK(ptr, size) \
	(((uintptr_t)(ptr) + (uintptr_t)(intptr_t)(size)) >= (uintptr_t)(ptr))
>>>>>>>> REPLACE
